topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture by welcoming students and setting out the core learning objectives concerning cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside the biological mechanisms that cause systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively destroy cancer cells by exploiting intrinsic biological defects such as hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and impaired DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on identifying driver mutations and inhibiting oncogenic kinases, detailing the pathways through which tumors acquire resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates target specific cell-surface receptors to eliminate malignant cells.

topics.label: Immune Surveillance and T-Cell-Directed Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate the relationship between cancer and host immunity, detailing therapeutic strategies that reactivate endogenous T cells or deploy engineered cellular platforms against tumors.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions in Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the broader clinical realities of cancer medicine by evaluating long-term survival trends, persistent biological hurdles, and emerging ethical dilemmas.
